package.title: 99 Airport Security Situational Judgment MCQs for ASF Preparation

questions.question: You notice a small bag left unattended beside a busy waiting-area seat. What is the best first response?
choices: Keep a safe distance and promptly notify the appropriate security supervisor or response channel
Open it to look for identification
Move it to the nearest counter
Ignore it because it is small

questions.question: A colleague suggests moving an unattended parcel to clear a walkway. What should you do?
choices: Do not move it; report its location and follow the responsible security personnel's instructions
Move it a short distance without opening it
Ask a passenger to move it
Cover it so people do not notice

questions.question: You see a person leave a bag behind while repeatedly looking around, but you do not know their intent. What is the soundest action?
choices: Report the specific behavior and location without guessing at the person's motive
Announce that the person is a threat
Follow the person without notifying anyone
Do nothing unless the person returns

questions.question: A nearby passenger says an unattended bag belongs to their companion. What should you do?
choices: Report the situation and follow applicable instructions rather than relying only on an unverified explanation
Accept the explanation and leave immediately
Open the bag to check whether it matches the story
Ask the passenger to carry it away

questions.question: You are asked to describe an unattended suitcase in a report. Which description is most useful?
choices: A blue hard-sided suitcase beside the east entrance, observed at about 10:15
A suspicious bag left by a dangerous person
A strange suitcase somewhere near the entrance
A bag that probably contains something important

questions.question: A passenger says a package has been unattended for several minutes. You did not see who left it. What should you report?
choices: The passenger's account as an account, along with your own observations
That you saw someone abandon the package
That the package is definitely dangerous
Nothing, because you did not witness it being left

questions.question: A child is separated from an adult and is crying near a public corridor. What is the best response?
choices: Stay attentive, reassure the child calmly, and notify the appropriate staff or supervisor
Take the child to a private room alone without telling anyone
Tell the child to search the terminal
Ignore the situation because no security incident is certain

questions.question: You notice smoke-like haze near a service doorway but cannot identify its source. What should you do?
choices: Report the location promptly and follow the site's emergency instructions
Open the doorway to investigate alone
Wait until you can prove there is a fire
Tell nearby people it is harmless

questions.question: A passenger points out a leaking container in a public area. What is the most appropriate response?
choices: Keep clear, report the location and observed leak, and follow instructions
Touch the liquid to identify it
Wipe it up with a cloth immediately
Tell the passenger to carry it outside

questions.question: A person leaves a package beside a bin and walks away. Which detail should you prioritize when reporting?
choices: The package's exact location and the person's observable direction of travel
Your guess about the person's nationality
Whether the person seemed unfriendly
A description of unrelated people nearby

questions.question: You see a person repeatedly trying a locked service door. What is the best response?
choices: Report the behavior and location through the appropriate channel
Challenge the person physically
Unlock the door to see what they want
Assume they are authorized because they look confident

questions.question: A passenger points to a bag and says it may be theirs but is unsure. What should you do?
choices: Keep the uncertainty clear, report the situation, and follow the applicable response
Tell them to open it immediately
Declare it abandoned without checking any process
Leave it because the passenger might own it

questions.question: During a patrol, you find a door propped open in an area normally kept closed. What is the best action?
choices: Report the door's location and condition and follow access-control instructions
Close it and say nothing
Enter the area alone to look around
Assume a colleague left it open for convenience

questions.question: You notice a suspicious-looking item, but a supervisor is speaking with someone. What should you do?
choices: Use the designated prompt reporting channel and provide concise facts
Wait until the supervisor is free, regardless of urgency
Post a photo of it in a public group
Ask untrained bystanders to investigate

questions.question: A person without visible authorization tries to follow an employee through a controlled door. What is the best general response?
choices: Do not allow access to be assumed; alert the responsible staff and follow access-control procedure
Hold the door open because the person is close behind
Assume the employee knows the person
Ask a passenger to decide whether they belong

questions.question: A staff member's credential does not appear to work at a controlled entrance. What should you advise?
choices: Use the authorized assistance process to resolve the access issue
Borrow another employee's credential
Force the door open
Wait for someone else to enter and follow them

questions.question: A visitor says their appointment is urgent but has no visible authorization for a restricted area. What is the best action?
choices: Direct the matter to the authorized contact or process before granting access
Let them enter because the appointment is urgent
Ask them to promise not to wander
Use your own credential to admit them

questions.question: You notice a controlled door has not latched after someone used it. What should you do?
choices: Report it and follow the site's procedure to ensure the access issue is addressed
Leave it for the next patrol
Wedge it open so it cannot jam
Assume the alarm will handle everything

questions.question: A familiar employee asks you to let an unfamiliar person enter a restricted area without checking authorization. What is the soundest response?
choices: Politely require the appropriate authorization check
Make an exception because the employee is familiar
Allow entry and record it later if asked
Tell the visitor to enter quickly

questions.question: A worker says they forgot their credential and asks to use yours for one entry. What should you do?
choices: Decline to share it and direct them to the approved credential-assistance process
Lend it because you will be nearby
Leave the credential at the door for them
Enter together and let them pass through behind you

questions.question: An employee appears to be following an unknown person through a controlled entrance. What is the best judgment?
choices: Treat the access concern seriously and report it through the appropriate channel
Assume the unknown person has permission
Shout accusations across the area
Ignore it because an employee is present

questions.question: Someone presents a credential that is visibly damaged and difficult to read. What should you do?
choices: Follow the procedure for checking the credential or referring the person for assistance
Guess the unreadable details and admit them
Keep the credential as a souvenir
Let them pass because the damage is minor

questions.question: A delivery worker arrives at a controlled entrance with a package and says they are expected. What is the best response?
choices: Refer them to the designated authorization and delivery process
Let them in to avoid delaying the delivery
Accept the package and leave the worker unescorted
Ask them to find an open door

questions.question: You find a credential on the floor near a controlled doorway. What should you do?
choices: Securely report or hand it in through the authorized lost-property or security process
Use it to test which doors it opens
Leave it where it is without alerting anyone
Give it to the first person who asks

questions.question: A person says a senior official has approved their entry but cannot provide the required authorization. What should you do?
choices: Seek confirmation through the authorized channel before allowing access
Accept the claim because the official is senior
Ask the person to name a second official
Let them enter while you make a note

questions.question: Your assigned post is briefly unattended because you need assistance with an access-control issue. What is the best approach?
choices: Notify the appropriate colleague or supervisor and follow coverage instructions
Leave without telling anyone
Ask an unauthorized visitor to watch the entrance
Disable the access control temporarily

questions.question: A passenger asks you to skip a screening step because they are late. What is the best response?
choices: Explain calmly that required steps must be followed and direct them to the appropriate assistance option
Skip the step to prevent a complaint
Argue about whether they planned well
Tell them to proceed without screening

questions.question: A passenger asks you to apply a screening rule differently because you share their background. What should you do?
choices: Apply the relevant rules consistently and respectfully
Make an exception to show goodwill
Ask other passengers to decide
Ignore the request and leave the area

questions.question: A passenger becomes frustrated when asked to follow a direction. What is the best first communication approach?
choices: Use a calm tone, explain the direction briefly, and listen to the concern
Raise your voice to establish authority
Mock the passenger for being impatient
Stop communicating and walk away

questions.question: A passenger complains that another person was treated differently. What is the most appropriate response?
choices: Listen respectfully and refer the concern through the proper channel without disclosing private details
Reveal the other person's screening information
Dismiss the complaint without listening
Promise a specific outcome you cannot control

questions.question: A person asks you to explain a restricted screening procedure in detail while others are nearby. What should you do?
choices: Provide only appropriate general guidance and refer detailed questions to an authorized source
Describe every restricted detail to satisfy curiosity
Post the procedure publicly
Invent an answer to avoid delay

questions.question: A passenger makes a rude comment about your colleague during an interaction. What is the best response?
choices: Stay professional, focus on the relevant issue, and seek support if needed
Insult the passenger in return
Stop applying the rules to end the exchange
Encourage nearby people to argue

questions.question: A passenger appears distressed and says they do not understand what is happening. What should you do?
choices: Speak calmly, clarify the immediate instruction, and seek appropriate assistance if needed
Assume they are deliberately obstructing the process
Give several complicated instructions at once
Ignore the distress and walk away

questions.question: A passenger offers you a gift to speed up their screening. What is the appropriate response?
choices: Decline it and continue according to the applicable rules
Accept it but complete the usual steps
Accept it if no one is watching
Ask for a larger gift

questions.question: A passenger's complaint is outside your authority to resolve. What should you say or do?
choices: Explain your limit honestly and direct the passenger to the appropriate contact
Promise that the complaint will be resolved immediately
Make up a policy to end the discussion
Tell the passenger nobody can help

questions.question: You recognize a passenger personally during a screening interaction. What is the soundest approach?
choices: Maintain professional boundaries and apply the same relevant process
Skip steps to avoid awkwardness
Tell others private details about the passenger
Ask for a personal favor in return

questions.question: A passenger asks why you are directing them to a different line. What is the best reply?
choices: Give a brief, accurate explanation appropriate to your role
Make a sarcastic remark
Invent a reason that sounds convincing
Discuss another passenger's private circumstances

questions.question: A colleague is speaking sharply to a passenger during a routine interaction. What should you do?
choices: If safe, help restore calm and address the conduct through the appropriate supervisory channel
Join in to show support
Record and post the exchange online
Ignore it in every circumstance

questions.question: You must give a quick incident report over a radio or phone. Which structure is most useful?
choices: Identify yourself and location, state the observed issue, then give necessary details
Begin with a long personal opinion
Use vague phrases and omit the location
Include rumors before the facts

questions.question: You are unsure whether a detail in your report is accurate. What should you do?
choices: Label it as uncertain or leave it out until confirmed
Present it as fact to sound decisive
Ask someone to invent a likely answer
Hide the uncertainty from the recipient

questions.question: A colleague asks you to repeat an instruction you received, but you did not hear part of it clearly. What should you do?
choices: Confirm the unclear instruction with the source before relaying it as definite
Guess what the missing part probably was
Tell the colleague a different instruction
Say nothing and let them decide

questions.question: You are reporting a person's movements. Which wording is most objective?
choices: The person walked from the west entrance toward the information desk
The person looked guilty and planned something
The person was obviously dangerous
The person was acting weird

questions.question: A report contains a time that you later realize is wrong. What should you do?
choices: Promptly correct the record through the appropriate reporting process
Leave it because the error is small
Change the record secretly without telling anyone
Ask a colleague to accept responsibility

questions.question: A caller gives you a detailed allegation about a person but no firsthand evidence. How should you pass it on?
choices: Identify it as the caller's allegation and provide any relevant details without endorsing it as fact
State that the allegation is confirmed
Ignore it automatically
Add extra details to make it clearer

questions.question: You receive two instructions that appear to conflict. What is the best response?
choices: Seek clarification through the appropriate supervisory channel before acting where possible
Choose whichever instruction is easier
Ignore both instructions
Tell others that one supervisor is wrong

questions.question: A passenger reports a concern while you are handling another task. What should you do?
choices: Acknowledge the report, assess urgency, and route it promptly without abandoning essential duties unsafely
Dismiss the passenger immediately
Promise to investigate later without recording details
Leave your assigned post without arranging coverage

questions.question: You are asked to hand over an unresolved issue at the end of your shift. What should you include?
choices: The current status, relevant observed facts, actions taken, and outstanding follow-up
Only your personal opinion of the people involved
Nothing, because the next shift can discover it
A conclusion without supporting details

questions.question: A colleague uses an unclear abbreviation in an incident message. What should you do?
choices: Ask for clarification rather than assume what it means
Guess from context and act as if certain
Repeat it to others as confirmed
Ignore the entire message

questions.question: A passenger gives a useful description of a person who has left the area. Which information is most helpful to relay?
choices: Observable clothing and direction of travel, with the time and location
A guess about the person's private life
An unsupported judgment about character
Only the passenger's emotional reaction

questions.question: An alarm or warning occurs in your area, but you do not know its cause. What should you do?
choices: Report the warning and follow the applicable response instructions
Silence it without authorization
Assume it is a false alarm and continue
Tell people the cause is known

questions.question: A small crowd begins gathering around a developing disturbance. What should you prioritize?
choices: Report the situation, follow instructions, and help maintain safety without provoking the crowd
Push through the crowd to confront someone
Encourage people to film closer
Make a public announcement about an unconfirmed cause

questions.question: You witness an argument that is becoming louder, but no one has made a threat. What is the best judgment?
choices: Report or seek assistance as appropriate, keep a safe distance, and avoid assuming a threat has occurred
Declare that an assault has happened
Join the argument to determine who is right
Ignore all escalation because no threat was spoken

questions.question: You hear a loud bang from an area out of sight. What is the most appropriate initial response?
choices: Report the sound and location, then follow the relevant instructions
Run toward it alone to identify the source
Tell others it was definitely harmless
Ignore it unless someone complains

questions.question: Someone collapses in a public area. What should you do first as a general judgment principle?
choices: Call or notify the appropriate emergency assistance and follow your training
Move the person immediately without assessing safety
Give medication from your own bag
Wait to see whether a crowd forms

questions.question: A person says they have lost a family member in the terminal. What is the best response?
choices: Gather the essential information calmly and contact the appropriate assistance channel
Tell them to search every restricted area
Ask them to post personal details publicly
Assume they will find the person without help

questions.question: A passenger tells you they feel unsafe but cannot explain why. What should you do?
choices: Listen, ask for relevant observable details, and route the concern appropriately
Dismiss the concern because there is no proof
Tell everyone nearby that a threat exists
Promise that no risk is present

questions.question: You notice a fire exit partly blocked by boxes. What is the best action?
choices: Report the obstruction promptly and follow the applicable safety process
Stack more boxes to make them stable
Leave it because the exit is still visible
Wait until an emergency to mention it

questions.question: A colleague asks you to leave a safety concern out of a handover because it has already been mentioned verbally. What should you do?
choices: Follow the appropriate reporting and handover process so relevant information is not lost
Omit it to avoid disagreement
Alter the details to sound less serious
Send an unverified rumor instead

questions.question: During a disruption, you cannot safely hear a radio instruction. What should you do?
choices: Request a repeat or clarification using the appropriate channel
Act on a guess
Switch to an unrelated channel without notice
Assume the instruction was meant for someone else

questions.question: A person appears to need urgent medical help while you are assigned to a post. What is the best general response?
choices: Alert appropriate assistance and coordinate coverage according to instructions
Abandon the post without telling anyone
Ignore the person to preserve your routine
Attempt treatment beyond your training

questions.question: A colleague reports an incident using an insulting label for a person. How should you record your own account?
choices: Use neutral, factual descriptions of what you personally observed
Repeat the insult as an established fact
Add a harsher label to make the report convincing
Remove all useful details

questions.question: A member of the public asks to see another passenger's private information. What should you do?
choices: Do not disclose it; refer the request to an authorized channel if appropriate
Share it if the requester seems concerned
Read it aloud so others can confirm
Send a photo of the record

questions.question: You accidentally send a work message containing sensitive information to the wrong recipient. What should you do?
choices: Report the mistake promptly through the appropriate channel and follow instructions
Delete your sent copy and say nothing
Ask the recipient to forward it to others
Pretend the message was intentional

questions.question: A friend asks for your work schedule and details about security routines. What is the best response?
choices: Do not share sensitive work details; direct any legitimate request to an authorized source
Share everything because the friend is trustworthy
Send the details through a private account
Give an approximate schedule to be helpful

questions.question: A visitor offers money for information about a security incident. What should you do?
choices: Decline and report the approach through the appropriate channel
Accept payment but share only a little
Ask the visitor to return later
Give a false story in exchange

questions.question: You notice a colleague has recorded an event time incorrectly. What is the most responsible action?
choices: Bring the discrepancy to the colleague or supervisor and use the proper correction process
Change the record without anyone knowing
Ignore it because the event is over
Copy the same incorrect time into your report

questions.question: A supervisor asks you to state that you witnessed something you did not see. What should you do?
choices: Decline to make a false statement and report only what you know
Agree to support the supervisor
Repeat what another person guessed
Write the statement and correct it only if challenged

questions.question: You find a wallet containing cash while on duty. What should you do?
choices: Handle it according to the authorized lost-property process and report the relevant facts
Keep the cash and leave the wallet
Give it to a random passerby
Take it home until someone claims it

questions.question: A colleague asks you to share your login so they can finish a work task quickly. What should you do?
choices: Do not share credentials; direct them to authorized access support
Share the login and change it later
Write it on a note beside the device
Complete the task using their name

questions.question: You see a work document left visible to people who do not need access to it. What is the best response?
choices: Protect it from unauthorized viewing and notify the responsible person or channel as appropriate
Photograph it for personal reference
Read it aloud to identify its owner
Leave it exposed because it is not yours

questions.question: A passenger asks you to delete a record of their screening interaction. What is the appropriate response?
choices: Do not alter records outside your authority; refer the request to the proper process
Delete it to avoid a complaint
Promise deletion without checking
Change the record to remove identifying details yourself

questions.question: You realize you made a procedural mistake that may have affected an interaction. What should you do?
choices: Report it promptly and follow instructions to correct or document the issue
Hide it unless someone notices
Blame the passenger
Alter the record to make the action appear correct

questions.question: Two tasks arrive at once: one is routine paperwork, and one is a new report of a possible immediate safety concern. What should you do?
choices: Promptly route the safety concern and ensure duties are covered, then return to routine work
Finish paperwork first because it arrived earlier
Ignore the report until the end of the shift
Ask a bystander to decide which task matters

questions.question: A colleague is handling an incident while you are responsible for another post. What is the best way to assist?
choices: Coordinate with the colleague or supervisor so help is provided without leaving your post unmanaged
Abandon your post without notice
Assume the colleague needs no help
Bring several unauthorized people to watch

questions.question: A group of colleagues gives inconsistent accounts of a minor incident. What should you do in your own report?
choices: Record your own observations and clearly attribute information from others
Combine the accounts into one certain story
Choose the most dramatic version
Leave out every detail

questions.question: You are tired near the end of a shift and notice you may have missed a routine observation. What is the best response?
choices: Tell the appropriate colleague or supervisor and follow handover or coverage instructions
Pretend you completed it
Make a guess in the log
Leave without mentioning the gap

questions.question: A colleague asks you to confirm a rumor about a possible incident. You have no firsthand knowledge. What should you say?
choices: State that you cannot confirm it and direct them to an authorized information source
Repeat the rumor as likely true
Add a detail you heard from someone else without attribution
Post a warning publicly

questions.question: A passenger becomes angry while your colleague is explaining a direction. What is the best way to support the interaction?
choices: Remain calm, avoid talking over the colleague, and assist if requested or needed for safety
Surround the passenger with colleagues
Interrupt with a threat
Record the interaction for entertainment

questions.question: You disagree with a colleague's interpretation of a rule during a live interaction. What should you do?
choices: Avoid debating in front of the passenger where possible and seek prompt clarification through the proper channel
Contradict the colleague loudly
Apply whichever interpretation benefits you
Tell the passenger to choose the rule

questions.question: A new colleague is unsure whom to contact about a reported concern. What is the best response?
choices: Direct them to the established reporting route or supervisor
Tell them to post it publicly
Guess a contact without checking
Advise them to keep it to themselves

questions.question: You discover that your earlier report omitted a relevant location detail. What should you do?
choices: Send a clear correction or addendum through the appropriate process
Wait for someone else to notice
Replace it with an unrelated detail
Claim that the location was obvious

questions.question: A visitor asks you to keep their security concern secret from all staff. What should you do?
choices: Explain that relevant concerns must be shared with the appropriate people and route it discreetly
Promise absolute secrecy regardless of risk
Tell the entire public area
Ignore the concern to honor the request

questions.question: You are given a task that seems outside your training. What is the most responsible action?
choices: Tell the supervisor what you can and cannot safely do, then seek guidance
Attempt it anyway to appear confident
Ask an untrained passenger for help
Refuse without explaining or seeking alternatives

questions.question: A routine task and a possible immediate hazard compete for your attention while you are alone. What principle should guide your decision?
choices: Prioritize prompt safety reporting while following instructions to preserve essential coverage
Always complete routine work first
Choose the task with fewer steps
Ignore both until another worker arrives

questions.question: A passenger asks for directions while you are monitoring an active access point. What is the best response?
choices: Give brief help if it does not compromise monitoring, or direct them to another appropriate staff member
Turn away from the access point for an extended conversation
Ignore the passenger rudely
Invite the passenger to monitor the entrance

questions.question: A colleague asks you to cover their post but gives no handover about an unresolved concern. What should you do?
choices: Ask for the necessary handover and confirm coverage arrangements before taking responsibility
Accept without asking anything
Assume there is no concern
Leave both posts unattended to find out

questions.question: You notice a colleague repeatedly overlooking a required check. What is the best action?
choices: Raise the concern through the appropriate supervisory or reporting channel
Ignore it because the colleague is experienced
Publicly shame the colleague
Copy the omission to avoid conflict

questions.question: A passenger asks you to make an exception for someone who appears vulnerable. What should you do?
choices: Show respectful consideration while following applicable rules and seeking authorized assistance for needs
Ignore the person's needs entirely
Bypass every requirement automatically
Ask unrelated passengers to decide

questions.question: You cannot verify a claim that a person has permission to enter a controlled area. What is the soundest decision?
choices: Pause access and use the authorized verification process
Allow entry because the person sounds certain
Let them enter and verify afterward
Ask them to choose which door to use

questions.question: After an incident, a colleague asks you to delete your notes because the situation was resolved. What should you do?
choices: Keep and handle records according to the appropriate retention and reporting instructions
Delete them immediately on request
Send them to a personal account
Rewrite them from memory to remove inconvenient details

questions.question: A passenger asks whether a particular person is being investigated. What is the best response?
choices: Do not speculate or disclose confidential information; refer the question appropriately
Confirm the investigation to reassure them
Share what you heard from a colleague
Make up an explanation

questions.question: You have completed a task but are unsure whether the next shift knows about a developing issue. What should you do?
choices: Confirm the issue is included in the appropriate handover
Assume someone else has told them
Leave a vague note without location or status
Wait for the next shift to ask

questions.question: A colleague is under pressure to hurry and suggests skipping documentation of an unusual event. What is the best response?
choices: Follow the applicable documentation process and seek help managing workload if needed
Skip the record because the event was brief
Create a vague record later from memory
Ask the passenger to write the official report

questions.question: Two people give conflicting descriptions of an event. What should you do when recording the accounts?
choices: Record each account with its source and note the conflict without deciding unsupported details
Choose whichever person sounds more confident
Merge them into a single account
Delete both accounts as unreliable

questions.question: A supervisor is temporarily unavailable, and you receive a report that may require quick attention. What is the best general approach?
choices: Use the established alternative reporting channel and follow applicable instructions
Wait indefinitely for one specific supervisor
Post the report on social media
Assume it is not important without checking

questions.question: A passenger has a disability and asks for help understanding a direction. What is the best response?
choices: Communicate respectfully, ask what assistance is useful, and follow the appropriate process
Assume the passenger cannot decide what help they need
Ignore the request to avoid slowing the queue
Ask another passenger to handle it without consent

questions.question: You have no authority to approve a requested exception, but the passenger says refusing will cause a delay. What should you do?
choices: Explain your role honestly and refer the request to the authorized decision-maker
Approve it anyway to avoid delay
Pretend a decision has been made
Tell the passenger to leave without explanation

questions.question: After a busy period, you are unsure whether an access concern was fully resolved. What should you do?
choices: Check the status through the proper handover or reporting channel
Assume it was resolved because time has passed
Erase your notes to avoid duplication
Ask an uninvolved passenger what happened

questions.question: A colleague asks you to favor a friend in a queue. What is the most professional response?
choices: Decline preferential treatment and apply the relevant process consistently
Agree because the request is harmless
Ask the friend for a favor in return
Move the friend ahead without recording it
